meta.title: Technical Analysis — Trip Lever, Access Paths, and Licensing Structure
meta.note: Verified technical and regulatory findings. Each row carries the official or manufacturer source it was read from; rows sourced to a third-party guide are labelled as such in the source column.

findings.finding: A bathtub trip-lever assembly consists of an overflow faceplate with a lever, a brass linkage inside the overflow pipe, and a plunger/drop-cylinder that seats in the drain passage. Lever up = open (drain), lever down = closed (fill).
findings.source_label: This Old House — How To Replace a Tub Drain

findings.finding: A stuck or slow trip lever is first addressed by adjusting/cleaning the linkage; a corroded or fused assembly typically ends in full waste-and-overflow (W&O) replacement. The brief's 5+ plumbers declining removal-from-above is consistent with a fused/corroded assembly rather than a simple linkage adjustment.
findings.source_label: This Old House (adjust steps); r/Plumbing stuck trip-lever thread (anecdotal)

findings.topic: Why access from below is the standard fallback
findings.finding: Manufacturer installation instructions show the W&O assembly is secured with a retainer plate and screws under/behind the tub, with the overflow elbow set against the tub wall inside the framing cavity — i.e., the assembly physically lives in the hidden cavity behind/below the tub. When the internals are fused, replacement generally requires reaching that cavity: from above via an access opening, or from below through the ceiling of the space underneath.
findings.source_label: Watco Manufacturing official trip-lever installation instructions (PDF)

findings.finding: The California Plumbing Code (2022 §402.10; 2010 §404.2) requires fixtures with concealed slip-joint connections to be provided with an access panel or utility space of at least 12 inches in the least dimension, unobstructed, so connections are inspectable and repairable. Tub W&O assemblies commonly use slip joints — so when the ceiling is opened below, fitting a proper access panel (rather than a solid patch) is the code-aligned outcome.
findings.source_label: IAPMO Answers & Analysis (UPC Ch. 4) + CPC 2022 reprint + 2010 CPC scan

findings.topic: Code — tub waste and overflow sizing
findings.finding: Bathtubs must have a waste outlet of at least 1-1/2 inches equipped with a watertight stopper; where an overflow is installed it must also be at least 1-1/2 inches, and the waste must be arranged so standing water does not rise in the overflow when the stopper is closed. Any replacement assembly must meet these dimensions — standard trip-lever kits comply.
findings.source_label: CPC/UPC bathtub waste outlets & overflows (UpCodes reprint; IAPMO/CPC arrangement rule)

findings.topic: Licensing — who can legally do plumbing + drywall in one job
findings.finding: Per CSLB's official guidance, a C-36 contractor may contract only plumbing work; a B General Building contractor is the appropriate prime when a job requires more than two types of work (e.g., plumbing + drywall), and a B cannot legally contract a job involving only one trade. Therefore the brief's all-in-one requirement maps to: B-licensed GC prime (hiring C-36 plumbing + C-9 drywall subs), or a license combining B + C-36 (e.g., Ace #829071, We Do Construction #1096552) with a drywall sub for the ceiling.
findings.source_label: CSLB — Find A Licensed Contractor / License Classifications (official)

findings.finding: Published 2026 ranges: bathtub plumbing repairs $100–$700+ (HomeGuide); tub drain replacement ~$700 with easy access, $500–$1,025 with difficult access (Angi); drywall patching adds $300–$930 (Angi). The received quotes ($135 adjust; $550 lever/diverter; $614 W&O replacement) sit inside these ranges for their respective scopes; a below-access ceiling opening + patch is additional and not yet quoted.

Ceiling opening in the storage unit below an occupied unit implies: tenant notice and scheduling around the unit above, dust containment in the storage unit, contents protection/relocation, water shut-off windows, and leak-testing the new assembly before closing the ceiling. Providers documenting property-manager/HOA programs and occupied-space work (Ace, Heise's, SF Building Group, Bay Area Plumbing) are structurally familiar with these constraints.
findings.source_label: Provider sites: Ace (HOA/property managers), SF Building Group (occupied-space off-hours work), Bay Area Plumbing (landlord/HOA 24-7), Heise's (property maintenance division)

findings.topic: San Francisco permit rule for this scope
findings.finding: SF DBI's official page states: 'You need a permit before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall or buried in the ground. See exemptions in San Francisco Plumbing Code Section 104.2.' Replacing a bath waste and overflow means cutting into and replacing pipe that is then covered by the wall, so the exemption question has to be put to DBI rather than assumed.
findings.source_label: sf.gov — Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (DBI)

findings.topic: Who may apply for the plumbing permit in San Francisco
findings.finding: The same DBI page lists the licence classes that may apply for a plumbing or mechanical permit: A (general engineering), B after scope approval (plumbing work tied to a kitchen or bath permit on PermitSF can be approved immediately for B contractors), C4 or C36 for a plumbing permit, C16 for a sprinkler permit, C20 for a mechanical permit, and C54 for a shower-pan plumbing permit only. Contractors registered for Express Permits on PermitSF skip City staff review.
findings.source_label: sf.gov — Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (DBI)

findings.topic: Licensing threshold — when a licence is required at all
findings.finding: Business and Professions Code §7048 exempts work only where the aggregate contract price is under $1,000, the work is casual, minor or inconsequential, and the work does not require a building permit. §7048(c) removes the exemption where the person advertises as a contractor or employs another person to do the work. Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective 1 January 2026.

findings.topic: Why a B licence can hold a plumbing + drywall job
findings.finding: BPC §7057(b): a general building contractor may take a prime contract for a project involving trades other than framing/carpentry only where the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts, or the B holder also holds the appropriate classification, or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor. Plumbing plus drywall is two unrelated trades. Six licences in the verified set hold both B and C-36.

findings.topic: Tenant entry notice before trades arrive
findings.finding: Civil Code §1954 permits entry to make necessary or agreed repairs. Except in an emergency, entry must be during normal business hours unless the tenant consents at the time, and written notice must state the date, approximate time and purpose; 24 hours is presumed reasonable notice, and six days is presumed reasonable if the notice is mailed.
